content.value_statement: AST-based refactors are hard to express with plain text search. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create and refine ast-grep rules.
actual_capabilities: Drafts ast-grep YAML rules for search, lint, and rewrite tasks.
Explains tree-sitter pattern captures and metavariable usage.
Suggests constraints that reduce false positives in common languages.
Provides validation steps for scan, debug, and update workflows.
Uses examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
limitations: Requires the target language, code pattern, and desired outcome.
Generated rules should be tested before applying fixes.
Does not verify ast-grep installation or project setup by itself.
Cannot guarantee zero false positives for every syntax variation.

use_cases.title: Refactor JavaScript APIs
use_cases.description: Create rewrite rules for API changes across a codebase while preserving reviewer control.

use_cases.title: Add Custom Lint Checks
use_cases.description: Turn team conventions into AST-aware lint rules with messages and clear match conditions.

use_cases.title: Review Risky Code Patterns
use_cases.description: Find unsafe or discouraged patterns with precise rules before manual review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Search Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ast-grep rule for [language] that finds [pattern]. Explain the match and include validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce False Positives
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this ast-grep rule for [language] to reduce false positives. Add constraints, test cases, and expected nonmatches.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Rewrite Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ast-grep rewrite rule that replaces [old API] with [new API]. Include safety checks and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration Rule Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-rule ast-grep migration for [framework]. Cover rule order, rollout strategy, CI use, and manual review points.

output_examples.input: Find console logging in a JavaScript project and suggest a safer replacement.
output_examples.output: A rule plan that explains the match, the replacement behavior, validation steps, and review precautions.

output_examples.input: Create a Python rule that flags broad exception handling without matching typed exceptions.
output_examples.output: A lint rule outline with match logic, expected matches, expected nonmatches, and a clear reviewer message.

output_examples.input: Plan a Go modernization rule for replacing a printing call with a logging call.
output_examples.output: A rewrite approach with scope limits, test examples, and guidance for applying fixes in small batches.

best_practices: Start with a search-only rule, then add fixes after reviewing matches.
Test rules on small representative files before project-wide scans.
Document expected matches, nonmatches, and reviewer assumptions.
anti_patterns: Applying rewrite commands to a full repository before reviewing matches.
Using broad text-like patterns when node kinds or constraints are available.
Treating one passing example as proof that the rule is safe.

faq.question: What is ast-grep?
faq.answer: ast-grep is a code search and rewrite tool that matches syntax trees instead of plain text.

faq.question: Does this skill run ast-grep automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides rules and validation steps for the user or agent to review before running commands.

faq.question: Can it create auto-fix rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft rewrite rules, but fixes should be tested before broad application.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The reference material covers common patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.

faq.question: Can it replace a full linter?
faq.answer: No. It helps create targeted AST rules that can complement existing lint and review tools.

faq.question: How should teams validate a new rule?
faq.answer: Use small fixtures with expected matches and nonmatches, then review scan results before applying fixes.
